name: Vehicle Tuning
description:
The per-vehicle feel sheet: acceleration curve, grip, drift tendency, and steering response, stored as named presets and applied on top of movement.vehicle_basic's stock handling. It exists because two cars sharing the same VehicleBasic should not drive the same, and the difference between them is data, not code. This component owns the parameter set and when it is applied — it re-asserts the tune on movement.vehicleEntered because VehicleBasic resets to stock handling on seat change. It does not own the physics integration (movement.physics_core turns the resulting numbers into motion) or the entry/seat logic (VehicleBasic). It also stores no progression: a part that improves grip is an economy and inventory fact, and what reaches this component is only the final numbers a garage system computed.

IT PUBLISHES THE WHOLE SHEET, not three numbers of six. It owns acceleration, top speed, grip, drift tendency and steering response — and declared only the first two as `effective*`, so the three that decide how a car CORNERS had no published form at all. A consumer needing them would have read something undeclared, which is the same defect as declaring an output nothing publishes, inverted: a value that exists and no contract mentions. Six inputs, six resolved outputs.

The resolved numbers are what a reader wants rather than the raw inputs, because a preset sits underneath them and a damaged car multiplies them. `effectiveGrip` is the number movement.vehicle_basic integrates against and progression.drift_scoring judges a slide by; reading `gripCoefficient` instead would miss both the preset and the damage.

inputs.name: presetName
inputs.description: Named tune preset to apply. Presets are how garages and part systems talk to this component — they install a preset name, never raw physics constants.

inputs.name: acceleration
inputs.description: Units per second squared at full throttle from standstill. Tuned against topSpeed: a high top speed with weak acceleration reads as a highway cruiser, not a sluggish car.

inputs.name: topSpeed
inputs.description: Ceiling on forward speed under power. Overrides movement.vehicle_basic's stock value while this tune is active.

inputs.name: gripCoefficient
inputs.description: Lateral grip multiplier. Below 1 the tail slides; progression.drift_scoring reads the resulting slip angle, so this knob indirectly sets how easy drift points are to start.

inputs.name: driftFactor
inputs.description: How much steering input converts to yaw while sliding. Distinct from grip: grip decides when a slide starts, driftFactor decides how steerable the car remains inside one.

inputs.name: steeringResponse
inputs.description: Steering angle ramp rate multiplier. High values suit twitch arcade handling; low values give the weighted feel expected from heavy vehicles.

outputs.name: activePreset
outputs.description: Which named preset resolved, after an unknown name falls back. A typo in a tune should not stop a car driving, and the reader should be able to see which sheet it actually got.

outputs.name: effectiveTopSpeed
outputs.description: Top speed after all multipliers, including any performance degradation written in by combat.vehicle_damage_states — damage rides the same path as tuning so 'damaged handling' and 'tuned handling' never diverge.

outputs.name: effectiveAcceleration
outputs.description: Acceleration after the preset and any multipliers. Units per second squared at full throttle.

outputs.name: effectiveGrip
outputs.description: Lateral grip after the preset. This is the number movement.physics_core's `planar` scrubs sideways velocity by, and the one progression.drift_scoring judges a slide against — below 1 the tail steps out.

outputs.name: effectiveDriftFactor
outputs.description: How much steering converts to yaw while sliding, after the preset. Distinct from grip: grip decides whether the tail goes, this decides what the driver can do about it once it has.

outputs.name: effectiveSteeringResponse
outputs.description: Steering ramp rate after the preset. High suits twitch arcade handling, low suits weight.
